extracted.intended_audience: NEA members, education employees, advocates, and policymakers engaging with federal education policy
extracted.subtask_description: The NEA Legislative Program enumerates the Association's annual federal policy positions (supports/ opposes) across four broad goals and numerous issue/subissue lines, to guide lobbying, member advocacy, and amendments proposed by members. It also defines the reference-numbering scheme and amendment process for proposing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference number scheme for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference numbers correspond to the topic (I, II, III, IV), issue (A, B, C, etc.), subissue (a, b, c, etc,) and amendment number (1, 2, 3, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please use the full reference number when proposing additions, deletions, or other changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-setting and amendment authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Our legislative program is set every year by our members at the Representative Assembly, the primary legislative and policymaking body of NEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members propose, amend, and ultimately adopt every bullet point; the NEA Standing Committee on Legislation gathers input and provides recommended modifications annually to the NEA Board of Directors. Members of the committee are appointed and serve term limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 1 — High-Quality Public Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative issues designed to address the many factors that impact the quality of public education directly in the classroom or school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This goal encompasses many issues including student learning, assessments, early childhood, parental involvement, youth development, safe schools, school choice, education funding, educator professional development, school modernization, special education (IDEA), postsecondary education, career and technical education, English language learners, federal impacted areas, and the federal role in education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 2 — Supporting Student Success
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative issues intended to create the best possible conditions for all children in support of both their development and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes children's health, safety, nutrition, child poverty/homelessness, youth employment, and substance abuse/dependency policy areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 3 — A Voice in the Workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative issues linked directly to some of the most basic employee issues faced by all education employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers public employee rights, retirement security, pension protection, and general employee rights, including collective bargaining and parity with private employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 4 — Good Public Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative issues related to ongoing concerns of national importance to both NEA members and the rest of the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses public health and well-being, human and civil rights, fiscal policy (credit unions, education & national security, taxation, trade), and other broad national matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.A Student Learning, Growth, and Development (general supports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal programs that provide assistance to public schools to achieve excellence and to meet the needs of students at pre-K through postsecondary levels, including ELL and special needs students; programs to enhance educational programs in all curricular areas; a 'whole child' approach; infusion of arts and design into STEM; advanced critical thinking and digital literacy; equity in funding/resources; assistance for educational reform that includes educator/parent/community engagement; optimum class size; programs to increase graduation rates and GED/high school completion; programs tailored to rural and urban communities; protections for student records transfer; inclusion of school library/media programs as core subject areas; and that science education be based solely on scientific theory and empirical evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also supports nationwide protocols for confidential student record exchange; counting students who take more than four years to graduate appropriately; and adequate funding for overseas schools for military dependents.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.A.a Assessments (supports and opposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports truth-in-testing (public release of content, validity, reliability, scoring); parental opt-out from standardized tests without penalty; state flexibility to waive annual testing and design less-frequent assessment programs; assessment plans conforming to NEA resolutions; alternative options for students with special needs; testing in language of instruction for multilingual students; sample-based assessment options (like NAEP). Opposes using standardized tests as mandated determinants of a student's future or as sole indicators of school success; federal requirements to make major decisions based on test scores or value-added models; narrowing curriculum through test prep; mandatory/coerced ASVAB participation; excessive educator time on testing administration; labeling schools as 'failing' for lowest performance; and use of standardized tests as an equity indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports flexibility and transparency in assessment design and administration, and accommodations for special needs and language instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.B Child Care and Early Childhood Education Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal programs to facilitate school readiness and federal assistance for early childhood education programs including Head Start; mandatory full-day kindergarten with resources; early childhood services by certified personnel accessible regardless of income; federal resources to enhance availability and quality of child care, preschool, before/after school programs; support for school-based or school-linked early childhood programs with community partnerships; coordination of nonpublic provider services with public school systems while ensuring standards and separation of church/state; stringent educational, health, and safety standards and regulation for preschool and school-age child care; incentives for employer-based quality child care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes standards, trained/licensed workers, nondiscrimination, and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.C Parental Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports positive involvement of parents/guardians/caregivers in schools; federal programs assisting parents in parenting skills and understanding child development; incentives for parental/community involvement; federal support for developing full-service public community schools and wraparound services addressing trauma and providing integrated family and health supports; programs assisting parents to ensure child success using research-based practices; ensuring student information is distributed to parents in the language they best understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposes forced conversion to charter status through 'parent trigger' legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.D Youth Development (juvenile justice, community service, school counseling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Juvenile justice: supports collaborative community efforts to reclaim youth, access to rehabilitation/support/educational programs for incarcerated juveniles, improved education on drug trade effects, national database for gang-related activities, collaborative programs among family/school/community/business/social services/law enforcement, separation of juvenile offenders from adults, reporting over-representation of minority youth, eliminating solitary confinement for juveniles, expedited confidential student record transfers between correctional and educational settings; opposes policies that encourage breakup of families or prosecuting/ detaining youth in adult criminal system. Community service: supports voluntary locally designed federal assistance for community service programs, oversight for liability concerns, opposes federally required community service as a qualification for financial aid and use of community service workers to replace employees. School counseling: supports counseling and pupil services by certified/licensed professionals, administrative structures to integrate counseling, grants to expand counseling, recommended staffing ratios by professional organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes rehabilitative, collaborative, voluntary, and professionally staffed supports rather than punitive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.E Safe Schools (supports and opposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal initiatives to prevent/combat violence and drug abuse; federal assistance for mental health services and student service professionals; district-level disciplinary codes developed with personnel/parents promoting non-discrimination; safety procedures for federal program visits; removal of violent/disruptive students to appropriate alternative public school settings (including students with IEPs) with continued educational services; removal from buses/other school areas with no cessation of services; federal programs promoting equitable enforcement of truancy laws; disclosure to school personnel of relevant documentation concerning violent students; provision of environments protecting from environmental hazards; legislation protecting from cyber-bullying; facility design promoting improved air quality; reduction/avoidance of pesticides and toxic chemicals with notification; prompt federal assistance for hazard identification/elimination; training and safety protection for personnel identifying/removing hazards; federally funded training for school/district health and safety experts; federal guidelines to operate hybrid/remote when public health deem unsafe; establishment of nuclear-safe and waste-free zones surrounding schools; bans on certain firearms sales; significant penalties for criminal actions involving weapons; restrictions (waiting periods, background checks) to ensure safer school environments; federal assistance for unified school safety crisis plans and emergency response systems; provision of trauma-based first aid and non-armament emergency supplies; protection from bullying, harassment, intimidation; reinvesting in mental health services; training in age-appropriate responses, cultural competency, implicit bias, anti-racism, restorative practices; properly trained personnel to promote restorative justice, de-escalation, crisis intervention; audits/reviews of discipline practices and transparency for school resource officer budgets; conducting audits for racial bias in discipline; strengthening accountability measures for school resource officers; promoting school-wide behavior interventions and restorative programs; support for basic security measures free of weapons (access control, panic buttons, internal door locks) with careful local consideration of other measures. Opposes discipline policies with predetermined consequences ignoring circumstances; discriminatory enforcement; legislation mandating arming education professionals; use of law enforcement/private security in discipline process; criminalizing school-age behaviors; Behavioral Threat Assessment programs disproportionately targeting Native students and students of color; federal funds used for school hardening measures (surveillance, metal detectors, fencing, security hardware); hiring private security in place of sworn officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favors preventative, restorative, health- and community-based approaches to safety, limits militarized or punitive security measures, and stresses transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.F School Choice (charter school conditions & overall stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports charters only under stringent conditions: authorized by democratically elected local school board (or accountable community-based authorizer where no board exists); full and independent written assessment developed with community input and publicly available; charter necessary to meet unmet student needs that cannot be fulfilled by other improvements; charters must improve rather than detract from local public school systems (no negative impact on racial/ethnic/socioeconomic composition, equitable access for special needs/ELL students, district operating/capital expenses, programs, services, facility availability); charters must provide a free, accessible, nonsectarian education for all enrolled students; charters must comply with safeguards identical to public schools (open meetings, public records, prohibitions on for-profit operation, conflict of interest/financial disclosure/auditing, federal/state civil rights, staff qualifications and certification, collective bargaining rights); state appeals of charter denial by districts should be narrowly limited to procedural grounds. Also supports parents' right to choose nonpublic education at their own expense and holding private schools that accept public funds accountable under federal law. Opposes federal funding to for-profit charter operators, public funding of sectarian schools or funding that enables nonsectarian nonpublic schools to provide services available to public school students, tuition tax credits for elementary/secondary schools, use of vouchers/certificates, federally mandated parental option/choice programs, preferential treatment for nonpublic schools receiving federal funds, and concealment of financing/materials/services received by nonpublic schools from public funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA's support for school choice is conditional and emphasizes public-accountability, nondiscrimination, and no adverse impact on public systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.G Education Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports exclusion of state/local taxes from federal taxation to maintain support for public education; federal funding via general aid and categorical assistance; adequate funding for a wide range of school support programs (aid for disadvantaged, ELL, disability services, gifted/talented, CTE, immigrant/migrant/refugee education, medically fragile students, desegregation, languages & international studies, American Indian/Alaska Native/Native Hawaiian institutions, gender identity & LGBTQ equity programs, magnet schools, arts in education, child nutrition, school-based health and mental health services, technology, construction/repair, impact aid, school libraries, TRIO/Gear Up); greater funding of federal programs that reduce state/local resources available for public education; use of latest federal census data for fund distribution; a federal census that contributes to fair/accurate distribution; federal funding for postsecondary education and student financial assistance to ensure access regardless of means; support for HBCUs, HSIs, Tribal colleges, and developing institutions; federal partnership role redirecting national priorities to substantially increase federal education funding; grants to support vital research functions; government-funded research on AI impacts in education; efforts to ensure stable, equitable funding of public schools historically receiving revenues from federal/state lands and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposes withholding funds from or penalizing districts that refuse cooperation with DoD testing, provision of federal funding to discriminatory institutions, federal control of local schools, diverting public funds to nonpublic schools, any program requiring reduction/elimination of due process/job protections as condition for federal funds, and misuse of federal funds by districts/institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.H Educator Professional Development (including recruitment & retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports funding for induction programs for new educators; establishment and funding of PD opportunities designed/directed by educators; initiatives to support development of cultural competence among educators; national efforts to professionalize education; programs for peer-to-peer professional learning; staff development and in-service training for all education employees; access to high-quality interactive PD in digital learning integration; state/local paraeducator certification programs with required training provided by districts; requirements for state credentialing of participating nonpublic school personnel; assurance of PD for all postsecondary members; federal initiatives that respect state certification requirements; training that defines the school-to-prison pipeline and addresses educational trauma and communications strategies. Supports recruitment/retention policies to encourage diversity, scholarships and loan forgiveness, paid residency programs for beginning educators, financial support during student teaching, initiatives to enhance compensation and affordable housing options for educators, and establishing an Education Support Professional Bill of Rights (living wage, retirement, healthcare, safety, paid leave, paid PD, protections from privatization, right to organize). Opposes federal programs that would weaken state credentialing/licensure and arbitrary mandatory requirements for paraprofessionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes educator-led PD, adequate compensation/supports, culturally competent/training addressing trauma and pipeline issues, and protections for educator rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.I School Modernization (education technology, equipment, materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports modernization initiatives including education technology, equipment, and materials to support teaching and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes ensuring equitable access and appropriate professional development for use of technology (implicit from other program lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: I.J IDEA Special Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports provisions and federal programs related to Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) special education services and protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on adequate funding, access to appropriate services, and safeguards for students with disabilities (implicit across the program).

rubrics_metrics.name: I.K Postsecondary Education (including adult education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal policies for postsecondary education, adult education, student financial assistance, and programs that reduce or eliminate tuition costs in public higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also supports institutional, scholar, and student support programs and support for minority-serving institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.L Career and Technical Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal programs for career and technical education providing vocational and career pathways for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes equitable access and integration with broader educational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.M English Language Learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports education programs that ensure equitable educational opportunities for English Language Learners and migrant students, regardless of immigration status; allowing testing in language of instruction when at least half of instruction occurs in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes equitable access to curriculum, assessments, and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.N Federal Impacted Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports adequate funding and programs for areas federally impacted (e.g., military base communities, federal lands) to ensure education quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes impact aid and special funding considerations for affected districts and overseas schools for dependents of military personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.O Federal Role in Education (including block grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the appropriate federal role in education policy and funding, including views on block grants and federal assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA supports a significant federal partnership role and cautions against undue federal control of local schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.A Children's Health (including school nurses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports policies and funding to ensure children's health services in schools, including school nurses and health-related programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of broader Supporting Student Success goal to create conditions for student development.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.B Children's Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports policies to protect children's physical safety in and out of school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prevention of violence, emergency preparedness, and supports aligned with Safe Schools lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.C Children's Nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal programs ensuring child nutrition, including school meal programs and related supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to address hunger and support learning readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.D Child Poverty / Homelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports policies addressing child poverty and homelessness that affect student well-being and educational access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes supports to reduce barriers to school attendance and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.E Youth Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports policies that provide youth employment opportunities while enhancing academic experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes voluntary community service and employment training programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: II.F Substance Abuse / Dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports prevention and treatment policies for substance abuse and dependency affecting students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes educational programs about the effects of illegal drug trade and supports rehabilitative services.

rubrics_metrics.name: III.A Public Employee Rights (including parity and union regulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports public employee rights, parity between public and private employees, and appropriate regulation of unions to protect collective bargaining and employee protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers a range of employment rights for education employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: III.B Public Employee Retirement Security
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports policies that protect retirement security for public education employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes opposing actions that would weaken pensions or retirement benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: III.C Pension Fund Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports protection of pension funds and safeguards against threats to pension solvency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes opposing misuse or diversion of pension assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: III.D General Employee Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports basic employee rights for all education employees, including workplace safety, due process, and fair compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces educator workplace protections across NEA policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: IV.A Public Health and Well-Being (including housing, environment, healthcare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports federal policies on affordable housing, culture/communications, energy, environment, healthcare, jobs & economy, senior citizens, social security, and related public health/well-being matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA frames these as intersecting with education and member/family welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: IV.B Human and Civil Rights (including voting & election reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports protections for school children and the general public on equal rights, nondiscrimination, protection from violence, specific populations, privacy, freedom of information, governmental intervention, and reinstatement/strengthening of voting rights and election processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific voting/election reform positions include support for reauthorization and full enforcement of the Voting Rights Act; equal voter access/enfranchisement; anonymous voting records for disputes; transparent disclosure of vote counting processes; independent/nonpartisan oversight/audits; public ownership of voting systems (including software); election day federal holidays; campaign finance amendments and disclosure reforms; restoration of voting rights for formerly incarcerated citizens; automatic voter registration and vote-by-mail; expanded voting hours and accommodations for disabilities; treating Tribal IDs like state IDs; language assistance on Election Day; opposing voter ID and restrictions that suppress participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IV.C Fiscal Policy (credit unions, education & national security, taxation, trade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions on fiscal policy include preserving independence of credit unions; public input/consultation during trade agreement negotiation; social charters guaranteeing human rights/environmental/union protections in trade; strengthening national security through education funding and sound economy; opposing military/economic assistance to governments permitting human rights violations; opposing federal funding that extends arms race into outer space; supporting progressive taxation to fund national needs including education; supporting tax provisions that provide relief/benefits to educators (miscellaneous deductions, tax credits for educational materials, exemption for certain benefits); advocating restoring estate tax to fund education; opposing unfair tax loopholes and constitutional amendments limiting taxes or federal budget; opposing shifting financing burdens to low/middle income; trade positions include opposing agreements lacking social charters or checks and balances and opposing Trade Promotion Authority ('fast track').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA links fiscal policy to stable funding for education and protection of social/economic rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural guidance for member engagement and amendment proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Members can propose amendments to the Legislative Program via the standing committee; the program represents adopted member proposals and on-the-ground experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NEA Standing Committee on Legislation seeks input throughout the year and via virtual hearings; members should follow the reference-numbering scheme when proposing changes and consult the stated process.
